_README: Facade strips (ROI x) for the test assets, as fractions of image width.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: roi_x restricts which horizontals feed the yaw, and on a
corner view that choice IS the correction -- one camera rotation can level one
wall, never two. A blanket 20-80% strip is not an application of the feature,
it is a default that straddles both walls on exactly the photographs the
feature is for. Measured 2026-09-20: a strip read off the photograph by eye
beats the blanket 20-80% default by 0.364 deg of horizontal lean against 0.131,
on 11 corner views. Placing it needs somebody to LOOK at the picture.
FORMAT: "roi": [x0, x1] as fractions of the FULL image width; "plane" names
the wall chosen; "read" says how carefully -- see the warning below.
!! HOW CAREFULLY THESE WERE READ, because it decides what they are worth:
"read": "full-size"  -- the photograph was opened at full resolution and
the wall boundaries were read off it. Trust these.
"read": "thumbnail"  -- read off a 440px contact-sheet preview against a
percentage ruler. NOT VERIFIED at full size.
The one strip that WAS checked at full size (Platte) turned out to be wrong:
the thumbnail reading of 0.05-0.50 straddled the strongly foreshortened left
wall AND half the frontal facade -- the exact error this file exists to stop.
Assume the same of every other "thumbnail" entry until somebody opens it.
These are judgements about photographs, not measurements of code. Disagree with
one by looking at the photograph, not by reasoning about this file.

Platte.plane: the frontal facade (murals 34 and 36). Portrait image, three zones, not two

note: The left sliver is a wall seen almost edge-on -- the hardest case there is,
and measured 2026-09-20 the most interesting one. All three strips tried on
this photograph return essentially the SAME yaw (-42.8, -43.3, -43.1 deg),
so the strip barely moves the estimate here; what it moves is CONFIDENCE:
0.20 on the foreshortened sliver (116 lines) against 0.49 on the frontal
facade (480 lines) and 0.54 on the sloppy wide strip. The narrow, correct
strip is the one the confidence gate would refuse. It also starts the most
crooked (10.74 deg of lean against 8.25) and gains the most: 10.74 -> 7.85
in one pass, -> 6.15 with a residual-capped second pass.

Mariánské_Hory,_panelové_domy_4.plane: right long facade; gable end left of 0.48

Platte_1.plane: left wing, seen almost edge-on. Corner seam is at 0.33; the strip deliberately runs PAST it
note: Measured 2026-09-20, sweeping the strip's right edge. This asset is where the
strip genuinely changes the ANSWER, not just the confidence: the left wing wants
yaw +45 deg and the gable end wants -39 deg -- opposite rotations, as two walls
of a corner should.
strip     conf      yaw    lean in the left wing (1 pass / +2nd pass capped 10)
0-32%     0.33   +45.24    4.99 / 6.56    <- best single pass, but REFUSED by the 0.40 gate
0-68%     0.59   -39.66    8.28 / 8.23    <- the vote FLIPS; worse than uncorrected
So the strip does NOT want to stop at the corner seam. Everything from the seam
out to ~2x the seam gives the same yaw and buys back the confidence the narrow
strip loses; past that the other facade wins the vote and the wall it was aimed
at ends up worse than if nothing had been done. Place it wide of the seam, short
of the flip.
